entity: U. S. Department of the Interior
role: federal agency commenting on wildlife management
stance_basis: commends cooperation on Keowee-Jocassee lands but questions whether wildlife mitigation measures compensate for losses from Bad Creek Project
summary: The U.S. Department of the Interior is paraphrased in Section 9.3 as commending Duke Power's cooperative arrangement for leasing Keowee-Jocassee Project lands for wildlife management purposes, while simultaneously questioning whether the proposed mitigation measures would adequately compensate for the loss of wildlife productivity associated with the Bad Creek Project. The applicant (Duke Power) responded by describing the history and success of its voluntary cooperative wildlife management agreements with state wildlife agencies, citing population growth of deer and bear as evidence of effective mitigation.
complaint_summary: The U.S. Department of the Interior commends Duke Power's cooperative arrangement for leasing Keowee-Jocassee Project lands to the South Carolina Wildlife and Marine Resources Department for wildlife management, but questions whether the proposed measures would compensate for the loss of wildlife productivity caused by the Bad Creek Project.
